question: How did falling CO₂ give Antarctica its ice sheet?
answer: About 32–33 million years ago, CO₂ fell from about 1000 to 600 ppm. Less CO₂ trapped less heat, so Antarctic snow stopped melting in summer and piled up into an ice sheet. As CO₂ kept falling, the ice grew thicker.
move: Antarctica froze once CO₂ fell to about 600 ppm.
